newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan phone firms to share cable in industry shift.
newsitem.headline: Japan phone firms to share cable in industry shift.

text.p: A leading Japanese domestic telephone company, DDI Corp, announced plans on Friday to use an undersea cable to be laid by international carrier KDD in an alliance that could herald an industry shake-up.

DDI, Japan's second biggest domestic operator behind telecoms giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), said it had agreed to buy 20 percent of the transmission capacity of the cable, to be laid around Japan by mid-1999.
The cable collaboration with Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co is seen by analysts as the start of a fundamental realignment of Japan's huge telecoms industry triggered by deregulation.
A DDI spokesman said the company had agreed to buy 20 percent of the capacity from KDD but had yet to pin down the details, including the cost.
"We will negotiate over specifics and would like to sign the agreement in early 1997," he said.
Japanese telephone operators have long been restricted to certain segments of the market, such as local, domestic long-distance and international operations.

But liberalisation of the market, including a restructuring of the colossal NTT, is expected to force smaller telephone operators to seek partners to strengthen their position or risk seeing their business slip away.

KDD's new cable, to be built at a cost of around $900 million, will help meet growing Japanese demand for telephone services, including surfing the Internet, and give KDD the muscle to expand into NTT's domestic territory.
The cable will loop around Japan's three main islands and carry 1.2 million telephone lines, with voice and data transmission capacity of 100 gigabits per second.

NTT -- currently banned from offering international services -- is expected to announce the launch of international operations through a wholly owned unit in early January as part of its restructuring.
KDD will start offering domestic long-distance telephone calls next year.
The new undersea cable will provide DDI with a reliable transmission method. DDI currently relies on microwaves for transmission of voice and data and suffers from a lack of capacity.

Newspaper reports put the likely price for a fifth of the cable capacity at around 40 billion ($347 million) to 50 billion yen ($434 million), although industry analysts said the cost would probably be lower than that.
DDI has said it plans to invest between 50 billion ($434 million) and 60 billion yen ($521 million) annually to complete its own on-land fibre-optic cable networks by 2003.
A DDI spokesman said the investment could be reduced, depending on the progress made with undersea cable. ($1=115 yen)
